issue: M60 clojure deep round — CLJ-D20 (the lane's last regex)
note: `/^%(\d+|&)?$/` decided whether a `#(…)` head was a parameter reference rather than a callee, and it was the last regex reviews/regex-policy.md carried for clojure — registered with the note "mechanically convertible to a structural symbol-name check". It is a char scan now (`isAnonArgShorthand`), and the conversion is PROVED, not asserted: script/m14/tmp/clj-regex-equiv.ts runs the regex and the scan over every `sym_lit` name in three corpora (633 files, 187,678 symbol nodes, 13,363 distinct names) plus a 42-case adversarial battery (`%%`, `%&x`, `%0`, `%00`, `Arabic-Indic-digit-one`, `% 1`, `%1a`, a twenty-digit `%…`) and reports 0 mismatches. The accepted-shorthand half pins the observable behaviour (no `calls` edge for `%`, `%&`, `%1`, `%2`, `%3`); the boundary is pinned from the other side, where `%&x` and `%1a` are NOT shorthands and so ARE read as callees — two deliberately malformed heads, kept because a greedy filter is only observable through them.
